  > 1. Section 5.3 (heading and "not supported at a default or reference budget") and the Discussion sentence "Aggregate agreement hides decision-level failures only at small budgets" are true only for the tolerance-aware contrast, which is 0 at every reference budget by construction (the paper says so). On the strict criterion, which the paper calls the informative one near ties, Table 4 shows the contrast at the reference budget is 13.0 [7,19] points for Pima RF and 21.0 [13,29] for GMSC RF (r >= 0.99 yet strict share 0.87 / 0.79), and 5-10 points with intervals excluding zero in 8 more cells (results/tables/h1_contrast.csv). State both readings and set the heading, the Discussion sentence and intro (ii) to what the strict contrast shows. No new computation needed.
  > 
  > **may** (owner decides)
  > 2. Fig 3 (b),(d): row labels sit on the markers; put them as tick labels or enlarge.
  > 3. Section 5.4 is one ~35-line paragraph; keep the conclusion in the body and the thinning/probit numbers in Appendix C.
  > 4. Intro result paragraph repeats the abstract's numbers; add a motivating instance and a contribution list instead.
  > 5. Abstract: define "certificate"; say "reference budget" where d <= 10 (the default enumerates there).
  > 6. Remove process notes ("Title and abstract only were read") from reference entries.
  > 7. Scope: default-budget evidence is d = 16 and 20 only. A large-d tree-model extension with interventional TreeSHAP as the exact reference (Arrhythmia, d = 279, is supplied) would answer the objection; not required for a release version, required (or an explicit reason it cannot be done) for final.
  >
